name: find_receipt
description: @funny receipts researcher: finds the exact moment someone said something in a YouTube video, from the video's captions, without downloading any video. Searches YouTube with yt-dlp (`query`), reads each result's captions (manual Hindi/English first, else the original-language auto captions; cached per video in Documents/Helios/Receipts/captions, so a repeat search is instant) and fuzzy-matches `quote` across scripts: a Roman Hinglish quote finds Devanagari captions and the other way round ("Modi se achcha ek gadha better hai" finds मोदी से अच्छा एक गधा बेटर है). Returns candidates best first — url, title, channel, start/end in source seconds (padded 0.3 s), the caption text matched, a 0–1 score — each with `download`: the download_online_media arguments {url, startTime, endTime} that fetch only that moment. Check the title/channel/text of the best one before downloading; scores under 0.7 are near misses. Requests run one at a time and HTTP 429s from YouTube are waited out, so a search takes 10–60 s. Read-only; any phase. Then download_online_media {url, startTime, endTime} (GATHER) and use the clip as a `receipt` move with word captions.

query.description: What to search YouTube for: who said it and where ("KK Create Dhruv Rathee podcast", "Rahul Gandhi press conference vote chori H files"), or one YouTube URL to search in.

quote.description: The words as they were said, in Roman Hinglish, English or Devanagari. Shorter and exact beats long and paraphrased.

channel.description: Keep to videos by this channel or uploader (matched loosely: "KK Create" matches "Learn By KK Create").

lang.description: Caption language to read ("hi", "en"). Default: Hindi, then English.
